$$h=A\sin[n(t+\varepsilon)]+C$$

Note: The diagram is not to scale and you may assume that each tide reaches the same heights, for high and low tides.

solutions.question: 11(e)
solutions.latex:
Method 1:

$\text{RHS}=\dfrac{-3}{x}+4=\dfrac{-3+4x}{x}=\dfrac{4x-3}{x}=\text{LHS}$

Method 2:

$\text{LHS}=\dfrac{4x-3}{x}=\dfrac{4x}{x}-\dfrac{3}{x}=4-\dfrac{3}{x}=\text{RHS}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: for either LHS to RHS or RHS to LHS

solutions.question: 11(e)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: for asymptotes x=0 and y=4; 1: for two hyperbola branches in correct quadrants; 1: for shape and accuracy with x-intercept of 3/4

solutions.latex:
$f'(x)=6x^2-6x$

$f''(x)=12x-6$

$\therefore\ 12x-6>0$ for concave up.

$12x>6$, so $x>\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ concave up when $x>\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$f(x)=0$

$\therefore\ 2x^3-3x^2=0$

$x^2(2x-3)=0$

$\therefore\ x=0,\ \dfrac{3}{2}$

Stationary points when $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=0$, i.e. when $6x^2-6x=0$.

$\therefore\ 6x(x-1)=0$, so $x=0,1$.

When $x=0$, $y=0$. When $x=1$, $y=2(1)^3-3(1)^2=-1$.

$\therefore$ stationary points are $(0,0)$ and $(1,-1)$.

Now $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=12x-6$.

When $x=0$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=-6<0$ (concave down), so a maximum turning point at $(0,0)$.

When $x=1$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=6>0$ (concave up), so a minimum turning point at $(1,-1)$.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: x=0,1; 1: stationary points (0,0) and (1,-1); 1: nature of each

solutions.latex:
Point of inflexion when $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=0$ and concavity changes, i.e. when $12x-6=0$, so $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

When $x=\dfrac{1}{2}$, $y=2\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3-3\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2=\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{3}{4}=-\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\therefore$ point of inflexion is $\left(\dfrac{1}{2},-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

NB: Concavity changes either side of $\left(\dfrac{1}{2},-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$ at the turning point. There is no need to check the change of concavity since the question indicates there is a point of inflexion.
\exfigure{1035_q12e_s1}
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: two correct turning points; 1: POI and x-intercept; 1: overall shape; 1: concavity correct, either side of POI and at each end of the curve

solutions.question: 14(a)
solutions.latex:
Velocity: $\dot{x}=3t^2-12t+9$

At rest when $\dot{x}=0$, i.e. $t^2-4t+3=0$

$(t-3)(t-1)=0$, so $t=1,3$.

When $t=1$, $x=1-6+9=4$.

When $t=3$, $x=3^3-6(3)^2+9(3)=27-54+27=0$.

$\therefore$ at rest after 1 second, at position $x=4$ (4 m to the right of 0). Also at rest after 3 seconds, at position $x=0$ (at the origin, $O$).
solutions.edited_from_original: Guideline prints the working for t=3 as 3^3-12(3)+9=27-36+9=0; corrected to 3^3-6(3)^2+9(3)=27-54+27=0 (same result)

solutions.question: 14(a)
solutions.latex:
When $t=0$, $x=0$. When $t=3$, $x=0$.

$\therefore$ the particle has moved from the origin to $x=4$, stopped and returned to the origin.

$\therefore$ distance travelled $=4+4=8$ metres.
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: x=0 at t=0 and t=3; 1: distance 8 metres

solutions.latex:

solutions.question: 14(b)
solutions.latex:
Finding the primitive: $y=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+x^2-7x+C$

Substitute $(2,4)$: $4=\dfrac{2^4}{4}+2^2-7(2)+C$

$4=4+4-14+C$

$4=-6+C$, so $C=10$.

$\therefore\ y=\dfrac{1}{4}x^4+x^2-7x+10$

$A_{\text{lawn}}=2rl-\dfrac{\pi r^2}{2}=400$

$\therefore\ 2rl=400+\dfrac{\pi r^2}{2}$ $(\div 2r)$

$l=\dfrac{400}{2r}+\dfrac{\pi r^2}{4r}$

$\therefore\ l=\dfrac{200}{r}+\dfrac{\pi}{4}r$ (QED)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: area expression; 1: correct rearrangement to the result

solutions.latex:
$P=2r+2l+\pi r$

$=2r+2\left(\dfrac{200}{r}+\dfrac{\pi}{4}r\right)+\pi r$ (from part (a))

$=2r+\dfrac{400}{r}+\dfrac{\pi}{2}r+\pi r$

$=2r+\dfrac{3\pi}{2}r+\dfrac{400}{r}$

$=\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+2\right)r+\dfrac{400}{r}$ (QED)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: substituting l from part (a); 1: simplification to the result

solutions.latex:
Now $P=\left(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+2\right)r+400r^{-1}$

$\therefore\ \dfrac{dP}{dr}=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+2-400r^{-2}=\dfrac{3\pi}{2}+2-\dfrac{400}{r^2}=0$ (for possible maxima or minima)

$\therefore\ \dfrac{3\pi+4}{2}=\dfrac{400}{r^2}$

$\dfrac{r^2}{400}=\dfrac{2}{3\pi+4}$

$r^2=\dfrac{800}{3\pi+4}$

$\therefore\ r=\sqrt{\dfrac{800}{3\pi+4}}$ (since $r>0$)

$\doteq\sqrt{59.59}\doteq 7.7$

Now $\dfrac{d^2P}{dr^2}=800r^{-3}=\dfrac{800}{r^3}$

When $r\doteq 7.7$, $\dfrac{d^2P}{dr^2}=\dfrac{800}{(7.7)^3}>0$

$\therefore$ relative minimum value of $P$ when $r\doteq 7.7$.

[NB: Since the area is $400\ \text{m}^2$, the end points of the domain, i.e. either $r=0$ or $l=0$, which would produce zero area, need not be considered.]
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: dP/dr; 1: r approx 7.7; 1: second derivative; 1: conclusion that this is a minimum
solutions.edited_from_original: Guideline prints d^2P/dr^2 = 400r^-3 = 400/r^3 and 400/(7.7)^3; corrected to 800 (second derivative of 400r^-1 is 800r^-3); conclusion unchanged

solutions.latex:
High tide $=1.69$ m and low tide $=0.46$ m

$\therefore$ centre of oscillation $=\dfrac{1.69+0.46}{2}=1.075$ m

(the average is the median, for 2 scores)

Amplitude $=$ upper limit $-$ central value

$=1.69-1.075=0.615$

The period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{n}$.

From high to low tide is 2:54 am to 9:43 am $=6$ h $49$ min.

$\therefore$ period is $2\times 6\text{ h }49\text{ min}=13\text{ h }38\text{ min}=13.63\text{ h}\ \left(=\dfrac{409}{30}\text{ h}\right)$

$\therefore\ \dfrac{2\pi}{n}=\dfrac{409}{30}$

$n=\dfrac{30\times 2\pi}{409}=\dfrac{60\pi}{409}\doteq 0.46$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: period from high and low tide times; 1: n = 60pi/409 approx 0.46

solutions.latex:
The sine curve would start at the centre of oscillation and thus would have been 6 h 49 min before 2:54 am, i.e. midnight minus 3 h 55 min.

$\therefore\ \varepsilon=-3.9\dot{1}6$ (denoting the phase shift to the left)
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: start of curve at centre of oscillation 6 h 49 min before 2:54 am; 1: epsilon = -3.916
1: equation set up with h=1.25; 1: time 4:33 am
